transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Emma Liu (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Mike Patel (VantageHealth Eng Manager), Sarah Nguyen (VantageHealth TPM)

[00:00] Emma: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick sanity check, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Mike: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:05] Sarah: Good here.
[00:07] Emma: Great. So agenda for today — quick run through the pilot metrics, go over the dedicated sizing changes Carlos proposed, then agree next steps: load test and final autoscale settings. Sound right?
[00:18] Mike: Yep, that's perfect. Wanted to flag up front that our morning peak yesterday hit higher than expected, so I'm hoping we can go deep on burst planning.
[00:27] Carlos: Absolutely. I pulled the telemetry — I'll share screen in a sec — but top-line: overall GPU utilization averages look fine, like 60-65% during the day, but 95th/99th latency spikes correspond with short bursts where queue length jumps. That signals we need either more pre-warmed capacity or a faster scale-up.
[00:43] Sarah: Do you have exact numbers for the spike window? We need to map that to our customer-facing SLA window.
[00:48] Carlos: Yeah so the spike was about 7-9am PST, roughly a 15 minute window where QPS doubled from baseline 120 to ~250, 95th latency rose from 180ms to 1.1s, and 99th hit around 2.6s. KV cache hit rate stayed at ~78% so some of it is cold prefix miss.
[01:12] Mike: Hmm, that 99th is concerning. Our product team will push back if we don't hit sub-second during peak.
[01:18] Emma: Totally understandable. A few levers here: we can increase min_replicas to reduce cold start, lower target_concurrency so each replica handles fewer in-flight requests, and configure a small dedicated burst pool — pre-warmed GPUs that sit idle up to X% for short bursts. Each has cost tradeoffs.
[01:33] Mike: Cost is a factor, but for the pilot we can accept a little overhead if it proves stable. What's the fastest path?
[01:39] Carlos: Fastest is pre-warmed burst capacity + slightly more aggressive scale-up (lower scale cooldown and higher CPU/GPU scaling sensitivity). Practically speaking: min_replicas from 2->4, target_concurrency from 20->12, and a burst pool equal to ~20% of baseline capacity. That should bring 95th back sub-second in these short windows.
[01:58] Sarah: Can we set burst to auto-return when not used so we don't pay full-time?
[02:02] Carlos: Yes, it's a pre-warmed pool that charges only for the reservation, but you can size it small. Another model is to route non-critical queries to a smaller 7B variant as overflow — lower cost, faster startup — but needs model validation.
[02:16] Mike: I like the model-variant fallback idea as a cheaper option. Do we have telemetry on quality delta for the fallback model?
[02:22] Emma: Not yet for your prompt set — we can run a head-to-head eval. For the POC we suggested conservative approach: 1) small burst pool, 2) short scale cooldown (30s), 3) fallback to 7B only for non-authenticated or low-risk flows.
[02:36] Mike: Okay that seems safe.
[02:38] Carlos: Also wanted to call out KV cache warmup: if you have predictable prefixes (like templated prompts), we can prime cache during off-peak to improve hit rate. That reduces cold starts without more GPUs.
[02:50] Sarah: Interesting, would need an API to push up pre-warm hints.
[02:53] Carlos: We support a cache priming call in our SDK — it's low-effort, I can include sample script in the workbook.
[02:59] Emma: Let's walk the proposed numbers quickly. Carlos, can you read the suggested config so I can capture action items?
[03:05] Carlos: Sure. Proposed initial Dedicated config for pilot: min_replicas 4, max_replicas 24, target_concurrency 12, scale_cooldown 30s, burst_pool_reserve equal to 20% of baseline GPUs (for you that's two extra GPUs), fallback route to 7B model for non-critical queries, and cache-priming script added to the runbook.
[03:26] Mike: Max 24 seems high — are we expecting to hit that?
[03:29] Carlos: That's an upper bound to absorb unexpected sustained increases. If your traffic patterns are spiky but short, we'll never hit max; autoscaler will only scale to the level needed.
[03:38] Sarah: What about billing for burst? Is that on-demand or reserved billing?
[03:41] Emma: Burst reservations are billed as a smaller monthly reservation plus usage when consumed. I'll include the pricing delta in the spreadsheet we send.
[03:49] Mike: Good. Also, can we add region-based routing? Some of our traffic is east coast and that makes a difference for latency.
[03:55] Carlos: Yes, we can pin regional pools or route by geo. For now I'd recommend a single region for the pilot to reduce complexity, but for production we can replicate the policy.
[04:06] Sarah: Ok noted.
[04:08] Emma: Quick security check — any outstanding security/compliance asks? We sent SOC2 summary last week.
[04:13] Mike: Security team looked at it; they want to see audit log retention options and KMS integration for keys.
[04:19] Emma: We support customer-managed KMS and configurable audit log retention up to 13 months. I'll attach the security addendum and a one-pager.
[04:27] Sarah: Perfect.
[04:29] Carlos: Back to load planning — for the Thursday load test we'll do two runs: a baseline ramp to 120 QPS and a peak test simulating the double QPS for 20 minutes. We'll capture 50/95/99 latencies, GPU utilization, queue length, and cache hit rate.
[04:45] Mike: Do you need access to our staging tokens or should we hit the pilot endpoint?
[04:49] Carlos: Use the pilot Dedicated endpoint — we'll give a test API key scoped to the pilot. Please avoid production credentials.
[04:56] Emma: I'll send a meeting invite for Thursday 16:00 UTC and include the runbook.
[05:00] Sarah: Can Carlos share the scripts ahead of time so our infra can review them?
[05:03] Carlos: Yep, I'll drop them in the shared drive after the call.
[05:06] Mike: One operational question: if the autoscaler is slow and we see sustained 99th latency, is there an emergency manual scale option?
[05:12] Carlos: Yes, you can manually raise replicas from the console or via API. We also support a 'panic' route that immediately routes overflow to the fallback model.
[05:20] Mike: Nice. We'll document the runbook steps.
[05:23] Emma: Great. Any other blockers?
[05:25] Sarah: Not from my side. Just to confirm, you'll send updated sizing workbook today so we can review?
[05:30] Emma: Yes, I'll send it by end of day tomorrow (2026-11-04).
[05:33] Mike: Cool.
[05:35] Emma: Alright let's recap next steps. Carlos will prepare load test scripts and the recommended autoscale config; I'll send pricing delta and security addendum; Mike and Sarah will provide production QPS histogram and stakeholder list. Schedule the load test for Thursday 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC.
[05:51] Mike: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:54] Sarah: Thanks.
[05:56] Emma: Thanks, everyone — we'll follow up in writing.

Notes on transcription: occasional words may be garbled (e.g., 'KV' transcribed as 'kay vee'), some punctuation and speaker attribution are approximate.
